fixes.explanation: David is the name Paul gives. He says God's Son was a descendant of David according to the flesh. That's the human side of the family line. Paul puts it right at the start of his letter, and I bet he wants Rome to hear it.
Saul was a king of Israel (1 Samuel 11:15), so I get the mix-up. But Paul names someone else here. He says God's Son was a descendant of David according to the flesh. David, friend, not Saul.

Ahab was a king of Israel (1 Kings 16:29), so you're in the right neighborhood. Paul, though, says God's Son was a descendant of David according to the flesh. That's the name he writes. Ahab isn't the name Paul gives.

Miracles in Galilee is a fair guess, baker. But Paul's answer in this verse is different. He says Jesus was declared with power to be the Son of God by His resurrection from the dead. That's the line to hold onto.

Teaching in the temple is a good guess. But that's not what Paul writes in this verse. He says Jesus was declared with power to be the Son of God by His resurrection from the dead. Paul keeps it to that one.

The Law of Moses is a big deal in Scripture. But Paul doesn't say that here. He says grace and apostleship were given to call all those among the Gentiles to the obedience that comes from faith. Nothing about guarding anything in Jerusalem.
True. Paul says to them, "And you also are among those who are called to belong to Jesus Christ." (Romans 1:6) He counts the believers in Rome right in with the called ones. You got it, baker.
True. Paul says he and they may be "…mutually encouraged by each other’s faith." (Romans 1:12) So the encouragement goes both ways. It isn't just him encouraging them. You got it, baker.
Slow is nearly the opposite of what Paul writes. He says he's so eager to preach the gospel to the believers in Rome too. He's leaning forward, not dragging his feet.
The law of Moses is a big part of Scripture. But Paul doesn't say that here. He says he isn't ashamed of the gospel because it is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes.
Paul does mention the wise a verse earlier, so I see the link. But his reason for not being ashamed is different. He says the gospel is the power of God for salvation to everyone who believes.

Faith, from start to finish. Paul says the gospel reveals the righteousness of God that comes by faith from start to finish. Then he adds what is written: "The righteous will live by faith." That one word carries the whole verse.
